about: The open X-ray datasets of docs/research/xray-datasets-missing.md, one entry per set (LUMOS is fetched by grid/run-platform-fetch.sh as zenodo_lumos, record 18173664, whose landing grid/banks/lumos.json reads), read by tools/fetch_sources.py inside grid/01-fetch.sbatch; a figshare entry names the article's public API, from which the job reads each file's download URL, size and md5, and 'unpack' true opens each zip that came into raw/, since the bank stage reads files and not archives. Every entry lands at <data_root>/<id>/raw, the folder the registry entry data/registry/<id>.json names as the source's own; the state of each helper goes to <data_root>/<id>/fetch-state and the record of the run to <data_root>/<id>/FETCH.json. A field spelled null is not known; 'confirm' lists what a person reads on the page before the first run, and a route 'manual' is skipped with one printed line until the entry carries its link. The checksums the helper verifies itself (Zenodo's md5 per file, Hugging Face's LFS sha256) are not repeated here; 'checksum' holds a hash only where a page states one for a plain URL. The credentialed list is the opt-in list behind a PhysioNet login, whether a project is Restricted or Credentialed, which each entry's licence says.

open.about_the_check: Read 2026-10-21 (#44): the twelve URLs are batch_download_zips.py's, the same in three independent copies (N-Nieto/GenderBias_CheXNet, the alkzar90 Hugging Face loader's history, a Kaggle notebook), and differ from the list this entry held before in the second URL; NIH publishes no checksum for them (the script ends 'Please check the checksums' and the Box folder holds none), so the bytes are checked against the Academic Torrents release 557481faacd824c83fbf57dcf7b6da9383b3235a of the same release (its listing names the twelve archives images_001.tar.gz to images_012.tar.gz, 2.01 to 4.19 GB, beside two CSVs and the README; the torrent itself is fetched by the job, since this container's proxy refuses academictorrents.com, so its names and its agreement with Box's bytes are checked first there): lengths and SHA-1 per piece, after the download and before the unpack
